title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from p.13. C_0 is a category of 'ambient' algebraic curves of types (g,ν) with algebraic morphisms (finite étale maps, plus isomorphisms). Ĉ_0 is its profinite enlargement. In Ĉ_0 the isomorphisms are profinite completions of the C_0-isomorphisms: Isom_{Ĉ_0}(X,Y) ≅ Isom_{C_0}(X,Y)^∧ and Aut_{Ĉ_0}(X) ≅ Aut_{C_0}(X)^∧. These are profinite 'isotopy classes', i.e. elements of profinitely completed mapping-class (Teichmüller) groupoids.

On p.13 he shows the following.
- Every Ĉ_0-morphism f̂: X→Y factors as f̂ = u∘f̂_0 (formula 19), with f̂_0: X → Y' a Ĉ_0-isomorphism and u: Y'→Y a genuine C_0-morphism.
- This factorisation is unique up to unique Y-isomorphism, provided Aut_Y(Y') → Aut(Y')^∧ is injective.
- Composition is computed by an approximation argument (21)-(22). One writes ĝ_0 = wφ̂ with φ̂ in an open subgroup Ĥ_u that lifts through u (φ̂u = uφ̂'). Then ĝf̂ = (vwu)(φ̂'f̂_0), which again has the form (algebraic morphism)∘(profinite isomorphism).

This page gives the geometric interpretation.
- In (19), Y' → Y is a finite étale topological covering. Via the comparison ĵ (Riemann existence: topological finite coverings ↔ schematic finite étale coverings), it comes canonically from a finite étale covering of schemes.
- The profinite isomorphism f̂_0 is then a 'pro-morphism', or 'class of paths', between ℂ-points [X] and [Y'] of a suitable modular multiplicity (the moduli stack M_{g,ν}). Here 'path' means the profinite étale fundamental groupoid of that stack.
- Hence composition in Ĉ_0 unpacks into two operations: composition of paths in the fundamental groupoids of the moduli stacks of the curves involved, and composition of finite étale maps between algebraic curves, with (21) giving the rule for commuting a path past a covering.
- In modern terms, a morphism X→Y in Ĉ_0 is a pair: a finite étale cover u: Y'→Y and an étale homotopy class of paths in M_{g',ν'} from X to Y'. Equivalently, it is a path in the stack of covers (a Hurwitz-type object) projected to both moduli stacks.

He then observes that this purely algebraic description lets the category of 'profinitely isotopic' ambient curves be built over any algebraically closed field k, with no characteristic-0 assumption. The resulting category is functorial in k, so Aut(k) acts on it; for k = Q̄ this gives Gal(Q̄/Q).

The next page goes on to the following.
- Extensions of algebraically closed base fields give equivalences of categories.
- Isomorphism classes of connected objects correspond to the types (g,ν).
- Automorphism groups are (up to outer issues) profinite completions of Teichmüller groups.
- He names this the 'Teichmüller–Galois' category attached to the tower.

The purpose is to construct a Galois-equivariant categorical object, the precursor of the Teichmüller tower of the Esquisse, on which Gal(Q̄/Q) acts through outer actions on completed mapping class groups compatibly with coverings.
errors: 'Pas besoin qu'il soit de car. 0' is fine for constructing the category. But in characteristic p the fundamental groupoid of M_{g,ν} over k is not the profinite completion of the Teichmüller groupoid (wild ramification), so the identification of automorphism groups with completed mapping class groups fails, unless one restricts to tame or prime-to-p quotients.

The equivalence under extension of algebraically closed base fields claimed on the next page holds in characteristic 0. In characteristic p it fails for non-proper stacks such as M_{g,ν} (π_1 is not invariant under such extensions, cf. the affine line). Only the prime-to-p version is invariant.

The uniqueness of factorisation (19) relies on the injectivity hypothesis Aut_Y(Y') → Aut(Y')^∧, which must be checked (residual finiteness / stack automorphisms). It is assumed rather than proved on these pages.

ideas.what: Morphisms of profinite curve category interpreted as étale paths (classes of chemins) between ℂ-points of moduli stacks M_{g,ν}, via Riemann existence ĵ
ideas.modern_name: profinite étale fundamental groupoid of M_{g,n} with curves as base points; profinite mapping class groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); Oda, Ihara, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, fundamental groupoids of modular multiplicities)

ideas.what: Category whose morphisms combine moduli-stack paths with finite étale maps between curves, with explicit composition rule (21)-(22)
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid of a stack of covers / Hurwitz-correspondence category over moduli stacks
ideas.usually_credited_to: partially implicit in work on Galois actions compatible with covers (Hoshi–Mochizuki, Boggi, Lochak–Schneps-type settings); not standard as a named category
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions the Teichmüller tower, but its operations are cutting/gluing, not finite étale covers

ideas.what: Construction over arbitrary algebraically closed field k, functorial in k, hence action of Aut(k) (Gal(Q̄/Q)) on the 'Teichmüller–Galois' category
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on Teichmüller tower; Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory

missed.claim: Grothendieck's early Teichmüller–Galois category includes finite étale coverings between curves as morphisms alongside profinite isotopies (paths in moduli stacks). The Galois action is thus required to be compatible with covers, not just with the gluing/cutting operations of the later Esquisse tower. GT-literature mostly works with the gluing tower; a cover-enriched GT-type category is not standard.
missed.quote: la composition des morphismes des Ĉ_0 s'explicite en termes de composition des morphismes, d'une part dans le groupoïde fondamental de la multiplicité modulaire ..., d'autre part par les morphismes étales finis entre courbes algébriques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Suggests defining a GT-like group as automorphisms of a category of curves-with-covers. This connects to the congruence subgroup problem (Boggi) and to whether GT-type groups preserve Hurwitz correspondences.

missed.claim: Explicit remark that the category can be constructed over algebraically closed fields of positive characteristic, functorially in k, without developing what it is there (wild/tame issues).
missed.quote: peut d'ailleurs se faire sur corps alg. clos k (pas besoin qu'il soit de car. 0 !), et cette catégorie dépend fonctoriellement de k
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Points to a characteristic-p Teichmüller–Galois category, e.g. tame fundamental groupoids of M_{g,n} over F̄_p with specialization from char 0. This is a little-developed analogue of GT theory.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly an early form of the Esquisse Teichmüller-tower program. Two features add modest unpublished detail: finite étale covers included as morphisms with an explicit composition rule, and the explicit positive-characteristic remark.
transcription_corrections: Line 2-3: 's'il y a une variation (topologique) étales finis' should read approximately 'Y' est un revêtement (topologique) étale fini'.
'qui provient conséquemment' is likely 'qui provient canoniquement'.
'multiplicité modulaire convenable le, au sens' should read 'multiplicité modulaire convenable, au sens' (line break artifact).
'groupoïde fondamental de la multiplicité modulaire par les courbes ambiantes' should likely read 'pour les courbes ambiantes'.
